notes.2: While many candidates opted correctly, identifying feathers as the visible feature that can be used to classify a bird, some candidates incorrectly opted for wings.
notes.3: Many candidates understood that a bacterium has a cell wall. Some candidates incorrectly believed that an animal cell has a cell wall.
notes.4: This calculation proved to be demanding for most candidates. Candidates needed to convert the diameter of the frog egg cell into micrometres (2.5 mm × 1000 = 2500 μm). The diameter of the human egg cell is 120 μm. They then needed to divide the frog egg cell diameter by the human egg cell diameter to find the correct rounded value (2500/120 = 21).
notes.5: Many candidates appreciated that when a plant cell is put into pure water it gains water by osmosis and becomes turgid. Some candidates incorrectly believed that a plant cell gains water by osmosis and becomes plasmolysed.
notes.6: Many candidates understood that glucose enters the cells by both active transport and diffusion. Some candidates incorrectly believed that glucose only enters the cells by active transport. The lower curve, where no oxygen is available, contradicts this.
notes.8: Many candidates were able to describe the structure of DNA as two strands coiled to form a double helix. Some candidates incorrectly selected option B, each strand contains a sequence of amino acids.
notes.9: This proved to be a demanding question with most candidates giving an incorrect response.
notes.11: Many candidates appreciated that both light and chlorophyll are required for the leaf to photosynthesise and make starch. Some candidates incorrectly believed that the white outer region would contain starch.
notes.12: This proved to be a demanding question, with most candidates giving an incorrect response. Light intensity is a limiting factor for photosynthesis in the part of the curve where increasing the light intensity can increase the rate of photosynthesis.
notes.14: Many candidates understood that the ileum is part of the small intestine. Some candidates incorrectly chose the rectum or the colon.
notes.15: Many candidates were able to correctly identify the environmental factors that cause the largest increase in transpiration rate in a plant. Some candidates incorrectly believed that low wind speed and low light intensity were required.
notes.16: Few candidates understood that sucrose is translocated and is moved from source to sink.
notes.18: Few candidates were able to identify the correct order that red blood cells flow through blood vessels in the human body when travelling from the aorta to the right atrium of the heart. The key is 1 → 3 → 2 (arteries → capillaries → veins).
notes.19: Many candidates chose the correct option, although some candidates incorrectly believed that it was an example of passive immunity.
notes.23: Only a minority of candidates recalled that urea is produced by deamination in the liver.
notes.24: Most candidates were able to correctly identify X as a neurotransmitter.
notes.25: Only a minority of candidates recalled that cone cells are found in the fovea of the retina and that they detect colour.
notes.26: A few candidates were able to identify where vasoconstriction occurs in the skin.
notes.27: Most candidates knew that the hormones oestrogen and progesterone are produced during pregnancy by the placenta. The oviducts were a common incorrect response.
notes.30: A few candidates understood that lipase, being a protein, is coded for by a length of DNA.
notes.31: Many candidates were able to correctly complete the genetic cross and determine the chances of a daughter having the sex-linked condition.
notes.32: Many candidates were unable to identify the test cross that identifies a heterozygous parent, that is, tt × Tt.
notes.34: Some candidates understood that some xerophytes have leaves that are rolled up and covered with hairs.
notes.35: Many candidates understood that the energy being transferred along a food chain originally comes from the Sun. The word ‘originally’ is important here. Some candidates incorrectly believed that the energy comes from producers.
notes.36: Some candidates were able to correctly identify the pyramid of biomass for a forest.
notes.39: Only a minority of candidates understood that recombinant plasmids are inserted into bacterial cells to produce human insulin.
notes.40: Some candidates knew that a fungus is used in the production of penicillin.
notes.general_comments:
There was good understanding of: the characteristics of living organisms and variation.
There was some uncertainty about: magnification; enzymes; the rate of photosynthesis; the flow of blood;
translocation and deamination.
It is important for candidates to work methodically through information provided in questions, such as in
Questions 31 and 32.
